capabilities.target: spawn a researcher sub agent to investigate an account

inputs.source: Nightly batch of CRM account rows

instructions.note: The prompt says to retry or spawn a researcher and to keep going until every row is complete, with no stopping condition.
The design relies on the prompt to drive completion behavior and provides no structural limit on retries, runtime, or delegation.

elements.name: Shared enrichment API key and monthly quota

controls.name: Hard spend cap or quota partition for enrich.lookup
Maximum unattended steps, retries, and runtime
Bounded sub agent spawning and delegation depth

findings.title: Spend loop (TC6): unbounded retries and recursive delegation can exhaust the shared paid enrichment quota

forecast.watch_signal: Median steps per batch, retries per malformed row, and spawned researcher count rise; there are no current structural limits to fail.

evidence.observation: The prompt instructs the agent to retry or spawn a researcher and to keep going until every row is complete.
There is no maximum on steps, runtime, retries, or sub agents, and sub agents can spawn their own researchers.
enrich.lookup is billed per call and the API key and monthly quota are shared with sales and marketing teams.
The nightly batch contains 40,000 rows and about 3 percent have malformed company names that never return a complete result.
There is no spend alert on the enrichment account.

recommendations.action: Add a hard spend cap or partition the quota so this agent cannot consume the entire shared monthly allowance.
Enforce maximum retries, maximum unattended steps, maximum runtime, and maximum delegation depth, with failure handling for rows that never complete.
Add spend alerts and batch-level anomaly detection on retries and sub-agent creation so runaway behavior is noticed before the monthly quota is exhausted.

stride_coverage.rationale: No inbound protocol peer, authentication surface, or impersonation path is described in the provided artifacts for this batch job agent.
The artifacts do not describe tool definition changes or self-configuration, and the agent cannot modify its own config in the declared design.
The artifacts do not say whether batch actions, retries, and spawned sub-agent work are logged with attributable provenance.
The design calls an external enrichment API, but the artifacts do not state request minimization, payload contents, or logging treatment for outbound data.
The artifacts do not state whether the shared enrichment credential gives broader rights than the initiating business process would otherwise have.
The artifacts mention a shared key and quota but do not describe controls over key rotation, quota management, or update authority.
The artifacts do not say how the shared enrichment API key is stored, who can read it, or whether usage details are exposed.
The provided artifacts do not describe transport integrity, response validation, or request signing for the outbound enrichment API flow.
The flow crosses the trust boundary, but the artifacts do not specify encryption, minimization, or whether requests expose sensitive CRM fields.
The nightly CRM batch source is internal to the described workflow, and no external identity claim or remote peer authentication mechanism is part of this element.
The artifacts do not indicate whether the source of malformed rows is traceable to a system or user record.

rating.rationale: The design exposes a present property risk of denial of service through unbounded paid API use and recursive delegation against a shared monthly quota. No declared or verified structural preventive controls limit spend, retries, runtime, or sub-agent depth, so residual remains at the inherent floor. Forecast does not rise because there are no current controls whose decay would worsen the tier; reassessment is still required if task horizon, autonomy, or quota scope changes.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration in the provided prompt and runtime notes, not observed runtime behavior.
No runtime configuration, orchestration policy, billing guardrail configuration, or logs were provided, so control verification and action provenance could not be confirmed.

No protocol, credential storage, or API request schema details were provided, which limits confidence on information disclosure, spoofing, tampering, and elevation-of-privilege analysis outside the documented runaway-cost risk.
